Welcome to quizzers_astro!

We are passionate about astronomy, astrophysics, space exploration, and scientific innovation. Our goal is to explore the mysteries of the universe through the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.

We are interested in understanding astronomical data, discovering patterns, developing creative solutions, and turning scientific ideas into meaningful projects.

We welcome curious, dedicated, and creative participants who enjoy learning, researching.
summary:
COSMIC EYE – An Interactive Time Machine for Exploring the Infrared Universe

COSMIC EYE is a browser-based astronomy exploration platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Inspired by NASA’s SPHEREx mission, which studies the universe across 102 near-infrared spectral bands, the project aims to make astronomical observation and analysis more accessible.

The platform brings multiple exploration tools into one workspace. Users can search for astronomical observations, inspect images, compare observations from different times, and investigate possible visual changes. Its Spectral Explorer introduces the infrared wavelength ranges covered by SPHEREx, while the Object Investigator allows users to record coordinates, measurements, and research notes.

Built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, COSMIC EYE is designed to run directly in a web browser without specialised software. It combines astronomy education with interactive image-analysis features and personal research tools.

The long-term vision is to develop COSMIC EYE into a more advanced astronomy workspace that integrates genuine SPHEREx observations and supports deeper scientific analysis. The project encourages users not just to look at space images, but to explore, compare, investigate, and understand the universe.
details:
COSMIC EYE — An Interactive Time Machine for Exploring the Infrared Universe

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

COSMIC EYE is a browser-based astronomy exploration platform inspired by NASA's SPHEREx mission, which observes the entire sky across 102 near-infrared spectral bands, covering approximately 0.75–5 micrometres.

The main goal is to create a single workspace where users can explore astronomical observations, inspect images, compare observations and record their investigations.

The platform includes six main sections:

  • Sky Explorer: Provides an interface for searching astronomical observations and exploring available archive records.
  • Time Machine: Allows users to load and compare two astronomical images to examine visual differences.
  • Change Detector: Generates an experimental pixel-difference view to help users investigate possible changes between images.
  • Spectral Explorer: Introduces SPHEREx's wavelength coverage and the importance of infrared spectral information.
  • Object Investigator: Allows users to record object names, coordinates, measurements, observation details and research notes.
  • Science Centre: Provides educational information about infrared astronomy and the scientific motivation behind the project.

The website is designed to work directly in a web browser without requiring users to install specialised astronomy software.

2. What benefits does it have?

COSMIC EYE aims to make astronomy exploration more approachable, particularly for students, beginners and space enthusiasts.

Its benefits include:

  • Bringing multiple introductory astronomy tools into one interface.
  • Making image comparison easier to understand.
  • Introducing users to infrared wavelengths and spectral observations.
  • Providing a place to organise object information and investigation notes.
  • Encouraging curiosity, independent exploration and scientific thinking.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our intended impact is to reduce the learning barrier between the public and astronomical data.

Scientific observations contain valuable information, but accessing and understanding them can be challenging for beginners. COSMIC EYE aims to provide a more accessible starting point for exploring the infrared universe.

In the future, we hope to expand the platform into a more advanced observation workspace that can display genuine SPHEREx data products, support spectral analysis and help users investigate changes across different observation periods.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed as a lightweight web application using:

  • HTML5: Website structure and content.
  • CSS3: Layout, responsive design, colours and visual styling.
  • JavaScript: Interactive tools, image inspection, comparison functions and local data handling.
  • Browser File APIs: Loading and inspecting user-selected image files.
  • Local Storage: Saving investigation notes and records in the browser.
  • JSON: Importing and exporting investigation records.
  • NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA): Intended source for accessing astronomical observation data.
  • Netlify: Hosting and publishing the website.
  • Gamma: Assistance with preparing the project presentation.
  • AI assistance: Used during development for coding support, debugging, explanations and content preparation.

The project was developed using a laptop and a mobile phone for development, testing and publishing. No specialised astronomical hardware was required.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

The central creative idea behind COSMIC EYE is to bring several stages of introductory astronomical investigation into one accessible workspace rather than simply providing a collection of external website links.

The concept of a cosmic time machine represents the ability to compare observations and investigate how celestial objects may change over time.

The combination of image comparison, experimental change visualisation, wavelength exploration and object investigation gives users different ways to approach astronomical observations.

The project also emphasises accessibility by using a lightweight browser-based interface instead of requiring complicated software installations.

6. What factors did the team consider?

During development, we considered:

  • Accessibility: The platform should be understandable to beginners and usable through a web browser.
  • Performance: The website should remain lightweight and work on ordinary computers.
  • Scientific accuracy: Experimental comparisons must not be presented as confirmed astronomical discoveries.
  • Data reliability: Genuine scientific observations should come from authoritative astronomical archives.
  • Usability: Different tools should have clear purposes and be organised in separate sections.
  • Future scalability: The platform should be capable of incorporating more advanced astronomical data-processing features.

We recognise that the current version is a prototype. Full FITS pixel and spectral-cube visualisation, calibrated 102-channel analysis, reliable live archive integration and scientifically validated change detection are areas for further development.

Conclusion

COSMIC EYE represents our attempt to make infrared astronomy more interactive and approachable. Inspired by the scientific possibilities of SPHEREx, it provides a foundation for exploring astronomical images, understanding spectral information and investigating possible changes in the universe.

Our long-term vision is to transform it into a comprehensive public-facing workspace for exploring real infrared observations and learning how astronomers study the changing universe.
